subject: MAP and evaluation milestones — hosting mode & region prioritization
messages:
From: Sara Klein <sara.klein@brightline.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightline.com, devops@brightline.com
Date: 2026-07-15T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: MAP draft & region question — Brightline evaluation

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to pull together a concise MAP so we can align internal stakeholders on timeline and decision criteria. Two quick asks up front: 1) Brightline has a hard preference for US data residency (all production traffic must stay in us-east). Can Redwood meet that in Hosted mode or would we need Dedicated/Private? 2) We want a 4-week evaluation (POC) that includes perf tests at 100 rps peak and an integration test against our SSO.

Can you send a short MAP that covers milestones, what Redwood will provide (test harness, SOC2 evidence), who owns each task, and a target close date? Procurement needs this on the record.

Appreciate it — Sara
Sara Klein
Head of Platform, Brightline Retail
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Klein <sara.klein@brightline.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightline.com, devops@brightline.com
Date: 2026-07-15T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MAP draft & region question — Brightline evaluation

Sara — thanks, this is exactly the right level of detail. High-level answers up front:
- Redwoods Hosted API can be routed to a us-east region and meet US data residency for request/response only; however, for your latency/SLA and throughput target (100 rps peak with low tail latency) we recommend two paths: 1) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool in us-east) for predictable capacity and SLAs, or 2) Hosted with a Dedicated Capacity add-on (short-term reserved pool) if you prefer a consolidated billing entry.
- Private on-prem deployment is available but adds procurement and install time; typically not necessary unless you require full control over networking/air-gapped operations.

I've attached a first-pass MAP (MAP_Brightline_v1.xlsx) and a cost model estimate for the two recommended paths. Below is a suggested MAP and timeline — I can update to match your internal dates.

Proposed MAP (summary):
1) Week 0 — Kickoff (2026-07-20): Align success criteria, data residency confirmation, test dataset, SSO metadata. Owner: Brightline / Redwood (Monica)
2) Week 1 — Integration + Baseline perf: Redwood provides test harness + initial perf knobs. Owner: Marcus (Redwood SE) + Brightline devops
3) Week 2 — Load testing (up to 100 rps peak) + latency tuning: Evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated performance in us-east. Owner: Marcus / Laura (Redwood)
4) Week 3 — Quality & regression checks: Run representative prompts/traffic, storage/retention checks. Owner: Brightline + Redwood
5) Week 4 — Decision checkpoint (target 2026-08-17): Choose Hosted+Dedic reserve or Dedicated or Private, procurement kickoff. Owner: Brightline procurement + Monica

Target close (contract signature) if decision = Dedicated: 2026-08-24. If Hosted+Dedic reserve: 2026-08-10.

Attachments: MAP_Brightline_v1.xlsx (MAP table + owners), cost_model_estimate_q3.csv, SOC2_snapshot.pdf

I'll put Marcus and Laura on this thread to coordinate the perf plan.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Sara Klein <sara.klein@brightline.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightline.com, devops@brightline.com
Date: 2026-07-15T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MAP draft & region question — Brightline evaluation

Hi all — quick technical notes and what I need from Brightline to make the perf runs reproducible:
- Preferred: execute a paired run (Hosted in us-east w/ cache warmed) vs Dedicated (node type: 4xA100 equivalent) to show delta. I can run both in parallel during Week 2.
- I need a representative prompt set (1000 prompts, distribution of short/long), and a 1-hour peak trace target (desired 100 rps peak). If you can't share production text, synthetic distribution is fine.
- Provide SSO SAML metadata and a non-prod API key or a service account for the integration test; we'll isolate all test traffic and purge logs after the POC (and record retention policy).

Attachments stub: perf_test_plan.md (attached)

I'll schedule a 30-min pre-kickoff on Monday (2026-07-20) to walk through env and responsibilities.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Klein <sara.klein@brightline.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightline.com, devops@brightline.com
Date: 2026-07-15T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MAP draft & region question — Brightline evaluation

Monica/Marcus — thanks, this is helpful. Procurement wants SOC2 evidence (point-in-time snapshot) and an explicit statement about where logs and prompt content live during the POC. DevOps will provide SAML metadata tomorrow.

Two quick clarifications: 1) If we go Hosted + Dedicated Capacity add-on, will we get the same SLA and isolated billing? 2) What is your rollback plan if we find quality regressions during the perf run?

Sara
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Klein <sara.klein@brightline.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightline.com, devops@brightline.com
Date: 2026-07-16T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MAP draft & region question — Brightline evaluation

Sara — answers below and a short update after our internal sync: 

1) Hosted + Dedicated Capacity add-on: yes — you get reserved capacity in us-east with a billing line item that we can separate; SLA mirrors Dedicated for the reserved pool while it's active. We'll call this out in the quote.

2) Rollback / quality safety: Redwood will baseline model outputs on the representative prompt set and snapshot evaluations weekly. If we detect regression > agreed threshold (we propose 2% on top-line metric), we freeze rollout, revert to the last known-good model variant, and run a joint RCA within 48 hours. We'll include automatic fallback routing in the MAP so production calls go to the fallback variant during remediation.

Internal note (reply-all): Marcus — per our QA, let's prep two model variants for the run (v1-prod-like and v1-quantized) and enable KV cache warm-up. Laura — can you prepare the eval harness and embed the prompt set into the Drive link? I'll update the MAP spreadsheet with the final owners and the procurement timeline.

Next external milestone: Kickoff meeting on 2026-07-20 10:00 ET. I'll send calendar invites after I sync with Marcus/Laura.

—Monica
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Sara Klein <sara.klein@brightline.com>
Cc: procurement@brightline.com, devops@brightline.com
Date: 2026-07-16T17:42:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MAP draft & region question — Brightline evaluation

Thanks — Laura here with the eval plan deliverables and links. Summary:
- I uploaded the eval harness and the sample prompt set to the Drive folder (link above). Harness supports replay at target QPS and will produce latency histograms + token-cost reports.
- I'll run the paired Hosted vs Dedicated experiments during Week 2 and post results to the Drive as CSVs (latency_p95.csv, throughput_summary.csv).
- I'll include a short doc describing data handling during the POC (logs stored for 30 days in our us-east tenant, prompt content redacted in analytics exports unless you permit otherwise).

Action items for Brightline before the kickoff:
- Share SAML metadata and non-prod service account by 2026-07-19.
- Confirm whether you want Dedicated quote or Hosted + Dedicated Capacity by the Decision checkpoint (2026-08-17).

I'll join the kickoff on 7/20 and walk through the harness.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
